result: In 88 long COVID patients (33 bedridden) vs 34 controls, exploratory MRI/DTI found three mammillary-body volume phenotypes, altered fornix diffusion, and lower superior cerebellar peduncle volume, middle cerebellar peduncle FA and dorsal raphe/midbrain reticular formation volumes.
reason: Regions are mammillary body/fornix and brainstem-cerebellar, not thalamus/basal ganglia/choroid plexus; brainstem volume differences are the closest match (long COVID version); exploratory, no multiple-comparison correction.

result: On in-lab PSG, 28 long COVID vs 28 controls showed higher slow-oscillation power, faster spindle chirp and early spindle-SO coupling (linked to worse sleep quality); 19 ME/CFS shared some changes plus more alpha-delta patterns and raised infraslow sigma power.
reason: Objective PSG sleep in ME/CFS and long COVID; adds microstructure (alpha intrusion) that the finding detail flags as the more promising level; small samples, ME/CFS from a separate clinic.

result: 73 post-COVID patients vs 58 controls had higher trait fatigue and fatigability (alertness, handgrip) and amplified cross-domain state fatigue after cognitive load, emotional load and even relaxation.
reason: No brain-activity measure, so it does not test the motor-network finding; handgrip fatigability in long COVID fits the grip-fatigability finding as a long COVID version, though the grip protocol is not described as repeated maximal.

result: Clustering of 42 post-COVID cognitive patients vs 14 controls found two structural subtypes, one with reduced grey matter density in cerebellar lobules VIIIa/VIIIb and the putamen, plus medial frontal changes over six months.
reason: Putamen (basal ganglia) structural difference in long COVID on MRI; adds subgrouping and longitudinal data; small exploratory sample with healthy rather than recovered controls.

result: Multi-day wearable HRV was lower in 121 long COVID patients than 21 controls during daily activities and sleep (p=0.027), stayed lower for 24 h after exercise around VT1 (p=0.010), and nighttime HRV fell after intense or longer exercise (p=0.018).
reason: Same direction of lower HRV, but in long COVID rather than ME/CFS, with an exercise time-course; a long COVID version is extends, not replicates.

result: Multi-day wearable HRV was lower in 121 long COVID patients than 21 controls (p=0.027) and stayed lower for 24 h after exercise around VT1 (p=0.010).
reason: Finding concerns orthostatic testing (IOH, POTS) and MSNA, not ambulatory HRV; the paper is already covered by the neuro-hrv link.

result: Proteomics of the insoluble platelet-poor-plasma fraction in 18 controls, 20 pre-COVID POTS, 19 LC-IOH and 18 LC-POTS found few protein-level differences but extensive disease-specific PTMs, including AGE/oxidation on fibrinogen alpha in LC-IOH.
reason: Analyses the composition of the microclot-bearing insoluble fraction (like Kruger 2022), adding a PTM mechanism; does not measure microclot load, small preliminary study from the proposing group, amyloidogenicity only in silico.

result: Pre-pandemic POTS and long COVID POTS showed indistinguishable elevations in 14 of 15 plasma markers vs controls, including Caspase-1p20, IL-1b, IL-18, IL-10 and sCD40L, with IL-18 the top classifier feature.
reason: Finding covers T-cell exhaustion, myeloid shifts, EBV antibodies and cortisol; this inflammasome cytokine panel in POTS measures none of these and no atlas finding covers POTS cytokines (possible new item).

result: Pre-pandemic POTS and long COVID POTS showed indistinguishable elevations in 14 of 15 plasma markers vs controls, with IL-18 the top classifier feature.
reason: Finding concerns POTS prevalence and cerebral hypoperfusion in ME/CFS; the paper measures cytokines in POTS, with no ME/CFS cohort or haemodynamic measure.

result: In 25 long COVID patients, a two-day 6-minute step test showed low agreement and reliability with two-day CPET for VO2peak and neuromuscular complaints, and moderate reliability for perceived exertion and 24-h fatigue change.
reason: Method-agreement study with no control group; it does not report whether exercise provoked symptom worsening, so it does not test the finding.
